# **Assignment 6**

In this assignment, you will use R (within R-Studio) to:

+ Load an untidy data set
+ Tidy it using tidyr and dplyr verbs
+ Plot it with ggplot


**All file paths should be relative, starting from *your* Assignment_6 directory!!**

**This means that you need to create a new R-Project named "Assignment_6.Rproj" in your Assignment_6 directory, and work from scripts within that.**

First, we can load the *tidyverse* package and import an untidy data set

```{r, echo=TRUE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
dat <- read_csv("../../Data/BioLog_Plate_Data.csv") # you may need to modify this path to fit where this file is stored relative to your assignment 6 script
```

As you might be able to tell from the column names, this data set is all about the ability of various environmental samples to utilize different carbon sources. Each plate has 96 wells and in each well is a fluorescently labeled carbon source. You dilute an environmental sample and add it to each of the wells in a plate and then read light absorbance over time. Higher absorbance values indicate more utilization of that carbon source by the microbes present in the sample. 

```{r, echo=FALSE,out.width=300}
knitr::include_graphics("../../../media/Ecoplate1.jpg")
```

Here, we have real data from 4 environmental samples (two soil and two water samples), and their absorbance values at 24, 48, and 144 hours. These plate experiments were repeated at 3 increasing dilutions for each sample source.

# Your task is to Write an R script that:

1.  Cleans this data into tidy (long) form

#When I loaded this data into my R-Studio, it was already in long form but I will write a script that would do it longer??
dat_long <- dat %>% pivot_longer(
cols = c("Hr_24", "Hr_48", "Hr_144"),
names_to = "Time",
values_to = "Absorbance"
)
#This makes the data longer by increasing observations from 1152 to 3456. I would definitely say that is the long form.

2.  Creates a new column specifying whether a sample is from soil or water

dat_sample_type <- dat_long %>%
mutate(Sample_Type = case_when(
`Sample ID` == "Soil_1" ~ "Soil",
`Sample ID` == "Soil_2" ~ "Soil",
`Sample ID` == "Clear_Creek" ~ "Water",
`Sample ID` == "Waste_Water" ~ "Water",
))
#This code could probably be cleaner but I wanted it all spaced out to make sure I wasn't missing anything. 
#It's important to note that ` is different than ' and using the first one will tell R that it's looking at a column name.

#I also want to note that if there were other values not being specified, you should add .default = "whatever" so that other rows that don't fit a given condition will be accounted for. The catch all statement if you will.

3.  Generates a plot that matches this one (note just plotting dilution == 0.1):

```{r, echo=FALSE,out.width=600}
knitr::include_graphics("../../../media/biolog.png")
```

dat_sample_type$Time_Hours <- as.numeric(gsub("Hr_", "", dat_sample_type$Time))
#This command creates a new column in the tibble so that our hours can actually be charted as time rather than fixed points of data. 

ggplot(data = dat_sample_type, mapping = aes(x = Time_Hours, y = Absorbance, color = Sample_Type, group = Sample_Type)) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, span = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ Substrate) + 
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(50, 100, 150),           
    limits = c(0, 150)                
  ) + 
  labs(
    subtitle = "Just dilution = 0.1", 
    x = "Time (Hours)", 
    y = "Absorbance", 
    color = "Sample_Type"
  )
#This graph still isn't identical to the one we are given but I think there is differences between the data we have and the data used to create the sample graph so I got it as close as I could. I cannot identify an error I may have made that would make them look different from each other. 

4.  Generates an animated plot that matches this one (absorbance values are mean of all 3 replicates for each group):

This plot is just showing values for the substrate "Itaconic Acid"

```{r, echo=FALSE,out.width=600}
knitr::include_graphics("../../../media/biolog2.gif")
```

dat_means <- dat_sample_type %>%
  group_by(Substrate, Dilution, `Sample ID`, Time_Hours) %>% 
  summarise(Mean_absorbance = mean(Absorbance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
#First we need to calculate the mean absorbance of things.

dat_Itaconic_Acid <- dat_means %>%
  filter(Substrate == "Itaconic Acid")
#This creates the tibble to graph the mean absorbance over time for Itaconic Acid. Can be modified for any substrate in the data. 

anim_plot <- ggplot(data = dat_Itaconic_Acid, 
                    mapping = aes(x = Time_Hours, 
                                  y = Mean_absorbance, 
                                  color = `Sample ID`,        
                                  group = `Sample ID`)) +     
  geom_line(size = 0.8) +                  
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +                 
  facet_wrap(~ Dilution) +              
  theme_minimal() + 
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(50, 100, 150), 
    limits = c(0, 150)
  ) + 
  labs(
    title = "Absorbance Progression for Itaconic Acid",
    x = "Time",                    
    y = "Mean_absorbance",          
    color = "Sample ID"             
  ) +
  transition_reveal(Time_Hours)
  
animate(anim_plot, renderer = gifski_renderer(), width = 800, height = 450, res = 100)
